name: Valparaíso
facts: A South American Pacific port built across steep, colourful hills.
Historic funiculars link its hilltop neighbourhoods to the harbour.
photoAlt: A steep hillside port, with colourful houses, historic buildings and a blue Pacific bay.

name: Dubrovnik
facts: A walled Adriatic city that once led its own maritime republic.
Its old town stood in for King’s Landing on television.
photoAlt: A compact walled coastal city with red tile roofs on a rocky peninsula beside deep blue water.

name: Chefchaouen
facts: A mountain town in northwest Africa, inland from the Mediterranean.
Its old medina is famous for walls painted in shades of blue.
photoAlt: A blue-painted town beneath steep, dry mountains, with a slender mosque tower.

name: Luang Prabang
facts: A former royal capital where the Mekong meets the Nam Khan river.
Its Buddhist temples and colonial villas form a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
photoAlt: A green river valley with red-roofed buildings and temple roofs, surrounded by forested mountains.

name: Quebec City
facts: A fortified French-speaking city high above the Saint Lawrence River.
The turreted Château Frontenac hotel dominates its skyline.
photoAlt: A broad river below a North American city, with a large copper-roofed château on a bluff.

name: Hobart
facts: A southern island harbour city beneath a towering mountain.
Its port on the River Derwent is a gateway for Antarctic expeditions.
artist:
File:Franklin Wharf 2015.jpg: Michael fromholtz
derivative work: Georgfotoart
photoAlt: A marina full of sailing boats beside a low city and a large wooded mountain.

name: Cusco
facts: An Andean city more than 3,000 metres above sea level.
It was the capital of the Inca Empire.
photoAlt: A narrow cobbled street with white plaster walls, tiled roofs, heavy stone foundations and a church tower.

name: Bergen
facts: A rainy harbour city among the fjords of northern Europe’s west coast.
Its colourful Bryggen wharf was a Hanseatic League trading post.
photoAlt: A harbour city at dusk, with mountain slopes, islands and waterfront lights.

name: Jaipur
facts: A planned city founded in 1727 by a maharaja in South Asia.
Its old town is called the Pink City for its painted buildings.
photoAlt: A tall pink sandstone façade with many small projecting windows, decorative arches and domed finials.

name: Zanzibar City
facts: An island port off East Africa, once a hub of the spice trade.
Its historic Stone Town blends Swahili, Arab, Indian and European styles.
photoAlt: A densely built tropical port with flat-roofed buildings, a projecting waterfront and boats in turquoise water.

name: Guanajuato
facts: A colourful Spanish colonial city that grew rich from nearby silver mines.
Cars travel through tunnels beneath its narrow historic streets.
photoAlt: A dense valley city with brightly painted buildings, domed churches and dry green hills.

name: Gjirokastër
facts: A stone-roofed hillside city in the southern Balkans.
A huge fortress overlooks its Ottoman-era houses and the Drino valley.
photoAlt: A steep cobbled street between pale stone buildings with thick grey roofs, below green mountains.

name: Lüderitz
facts: A small Atlantic port on the edge of a coastal desert in southern Africa.
German colonial buildings line its streets near a diamond ghost town.
photoAlt: A dry coastal town with colourful colonial buildings, a church on bare rock and an Atlantic harbour.

name: Khiva
facts: An ancient oasis city on the Silk Road in Central Asia.
Its walled inner town is packed with tiled minarets and madrasas.
photoAlt: A walled desert city with sand-coloured buildings, blue domes and a tall tiled minaret.

name: Sucre
facts: A high Andean city known for its whitewashed colonial buildings.
Its country’s declaration of independence was signed here in 1825.
photoAlt: A highland city of white buildings and red tile roofs, with church towers and mountains in the distance.

name: Ouro Preto
facts: A steep former gold-rush town in the highlands of South America.
Its Baroque churches were decorated by the sculptor Aleijadinho.
photoAlt: A steep historic town with red tile roofs, white Baroque churches and rounded rocky hills.

name: Kotor
facts: A fortified old town tucked deep inside a winding Adriatic bay.
Its city walls zigzag up the steep mountain behind the harbour.
photoAlt: A red-roofed town and stone church tower beside a narrow blue bay enclosed by steep mountains.

name: Ålesund
facts: A coastal city spread across islands between the fjords of northern Europe.
It was rebuilt in Art Nouveau style after a great fire in 1904.
photoAlt: A compact city spread across rocky coastal islands, with multicoloured buildings and distant mountains.

name: Galle
facts: A fortified port near the southern tip of an Indian Ocean island.
Its seafront fort was built by the Portuguese and expanded by the Dutch.
photoAlt: A fortified tropical coastal peninsula, with red tile roofs, trees and waves breaking along the walls.

name: Saint-Louis
facts: A West African river-mouth city that was once a colonial capital.
Its old centre sits on a narrow island reached by the iron Faidherbe Bridge.
photoAlt: A low riverfront town with colonial façades and a slender mosque tower, seen across a wide river.

name: Ushuaia
facts: A port on the Beagle Channel near the southern tip of South America.
It is a main departure point for cruises to Antarctica.
photoAlt: A port below rugged mountains, with brightly coloured roofs beside a cold, sheltered channel.

name: Dunedin
facts: A South Pacific city at the head of a long, narrow harbour.
Its name comes from the Gaelic name for Edinburgh.
photoAlt: A stone railway station tower with an ornate pale clock face and dark masonry under a blue sky.

name: Antsirabe
facts: A highland city on a large island off the southeast coast of Africa.
It is known for thermal springs and colourful pousse-pousse rickshaws.
photoAlt: A sunny highland street with colourful two-storey buildings, a decorated tower and hand-pulled rickshaws.
